title: The first write that re-renders a board an older Intent rendered warns that an edit to a generated file is gone
body:
Found by ic on 2026-09-23 while re-reading the 3.2.1 CHANGELOG entries against HEAD, and confirmed by vc in the source at ca936e6c4. 0532 has landed (2e588c7cd) and is not yet deployed.

**What happens.** 0532 indents a multi-line board item's continuation lines. It taught `intent doctor` that a board rendered in the old shape is a stale render rather than skew: `views::skew` asks `board_rendered_before_0532` (views.rs:2367). The write path was not taught the same thing. `Facade::foreign_bytes` (facade.rs:17144) decides whether a file it is about to overwrite held bytes that were not the store's render. It excuses a difference only through `differs_only_in_renderer_owned_text` (facade.rs:17181), and never asks `board_rendered_before_0532` (views.rs:949).

So after an estate upgrades to a pair carrying 0532, the first write that re-renders a board view still in the old shape reports it as a lost edit. Any node's board write re-renders every board view, and so does a thread or issue write on a migrated board. The report reads `warning: overwrote bytes that were not the store's render -- an edit to a generated file is gone:` (render.rs:11227) and names the board. Nothing was edited and nothing is lost: the bytes were an older Intent's render. ic counted 14 boards in 7 estates that carry multi-line items, so the false alarm reaches every one of those estates on its first write after the second build all. This is 0385's false alarm again, arriving through the one predicate the write path does not share with doctor.

**What the fix has to do.** One predicate, "an older Intent rendered this", asked by both callers: `views::skew`, and `foreign_bytes` before it reports an overwrite. An old-shaped board is then re-rendered without a warning, and a hand edit in an old-shaped board is still reported by both. The drive: a board carrying a multi-line item, rendered by the pre-0532 shape, then any board write, which must print no overwrite warning and must still warn when the old-shaped board also carries a hand edit.
